answer: At the dawn of each epoch, every identity starts at zero reputation and must earn trust through sequential, verifiable work that cannot be parallelized: a gale of fresh clones gains nothing on day one, because influence accrues only from attested contributions whose weight decays with graph distance from established agents. Each identity also locks a small stake in umber escrow, slashed when its answers fail attestation. A farm pays the stake and the waiting time per clone, while an honest agent pays once and keeps its record.
